* **Reference Number:** POC-332858B095-32885
* **Requested Service:** Partial Knee Replacement / Unicompartmental Knee Arthroplasty (UKA)
* **CPT Code:** 27446
* **Provider:** Dr. [First Name] Reyes, MD, Orthopedic Surgery

Dear Appeals Committee,

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for my requested partial knee replacement (CPT 27446), which was issued on August 13, 2026. The denial letter stated that "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure." 

As a commercial plan member in North Carolina, my request is governed by the Carelon Medical Benefits Management "Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines: Musculoskeletal Appropriate Use Criteria: Joint Surgery" (Doc ID: MSK02-1125.1, Effective Date: November 15, 2025). I am submitting my complete clinical records, physical therapy notes, and imaging reports to demonstrate that I fully meet every criterion required for this procedure.

### 1. Direct Rebuttal of the Denial: Imaging Findings
The guidelines state that a unicompartmental knee replacement is indicated when there is:
> "Imaging evidence of significant joint destruction and cartilage loss, defined as Tönnis grade 3, modified Outerbridge grade III – IV, or Kellgren-Lawrence grade 3 – 4"

My knee imaging from June 2, 2026, clearly documents "full-thickness cartilage loss in the medial compartment with bone-on-bone apposition" and explicitly diagnoses "**Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 medially**." A Kellgren-Lawrence Grade 4 finding represents the most severe classification of joint destruction and cartilage loss, which directly satisfies the clinical necessity requirement.

The policy also contains the following notation:
> "NOTE: MRI should not be the primary radiographic test used to determine the presence or severity of arthritic changes in the joint"

To ensure there is no administrative barrier regarding the modality of the submitted imaging, I have enclosed the report and films for my weight-bearing radiographs of the [left/right] knee, dated [date]. These weight-bearing X-rays confirm that the advanced degeneration is strictly isolated to the medial compartment, satisfying the guideline requirement that:
> "Weight-bearing radiographs demonstrate only unicompartmental disease (with or without patellofemoral involvement), described as Kellgren-Lawrence grade 3 or grade 4 degeneration"

### 2. Comprehensive Compliance with Clinical and Conservative Care Criteria
The Carelon policy states that:
> "Elective medial or lateral unicompartmental knee arthroplasty (UKA)/partial knee replacement (PKA) may be considered medically necessary when ALL of the following requirements are met..."

The clinical records submitted by Dr. Reyes confirm that I meet every single one of these requirements:

*   **Failure of Conservative Management:** The policy requires a "Failure of conservative management of at least 6 weeks' duration (unless radiographs show Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 or diffuse modified Outerbridge grade III-IV changes)". Because my imaging shows Kellgren-Lawrence Grade 4 disease medially, this conservative management requirement is technically waived. 
    However, I have far exceeded this requirement regardless:
    *   **Supervised Physical Therapy:** I completed a 12-week course of supervised physical therapy (20 visits from April 8, 2026, to July 1, 2026) focusing on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion. This is fully documented in the enclosed physical therapy discharge note.
    *   **Pharmacotherapy:** I tried oral NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief.
    *   **Intra-articular Injection:** I received a corticosteroid injection on April 6, 2026, which provided only 3 weeks of partial, temporary relief.
*   **Severe Functional Limitation:** I have suffered from 24 months of progressive knee pain that is unrelieved by rest. This pathology interferes with my daily life to the point that I cannot climb stairs without assistance and am woken up 3–4 times nightly by severe pain.
*   **Physical Exam Metrics:** Dr. Reyes' physical exam shows that my range of motion is limited by pain, but my total arc of motion remains greater than 90 degrees, and I have positive provocative orthopedic testing on the affected side with stable knee ligaments.
*   **Absence of Contraindications:** I have no active local or systemic infections, no history of untreated substance use, a body mass index (BMI) of 29 (which is well-optimized for surgery), and I am a non-smoker.

### Conclusion
My clinical presentation, extensive 12-week failure of conservative therapy, and definitive imaging showing bone-on-bone Kellgren-Lawrence Grade 4 medial compartment disease make me an ideal candidate for a unicompartmental knee arthroplasty under your governing clinical guidelines. 

I request that you review the enclosed weight-bearing radiographs and clinical summary and immediately reverse this denial so that I may proceed with this medically necessary surgery under the care of Dr. Reyes.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Sincerely,

Harper Delgado  
Member ID: W927303466
